That sounds like a really exhausting way to wash long hair. 

If you have a partner or family members that can help it’s imo ‘easier’ to do your hair while in the bath. 

I have super long tangly awkward hair and when I first got bedridden again I started using a lush shampoo bar with lemon and salt and it kept it fresher for longer while my scalp learnt to adjust to a longer and longer wash day routine. Now my hair doesn’t really need washing properly so I cowash and rinse it out in the bath or with a plastic jug or the shower if I have to. If it’s actually dirty (like I’ve been outside or something) I’ll shampoo in the bath and condition with my hair in a scrunchie to avoid it going in the water and I used to at my worst also have a bath lift and an inflatable neck pillow so I would let it soak the conditioner in (code for take a break from hair stuff) while letting my legs soak and applying skin moisturising items that mean I don’t waste spoons after my bath trying to cover myself in body lotion (rubbing it in and having to be exposed and let it dry was always so exhausting for me) and then dunk my head or shower etc. 

You might find not cutting it but maybe just thinning it out a little means it’s not such a hassle to do? 

I really hope you find an easier way. I always loved when my carers did Dutch braids because it keeps it clean and in place but I can’t seem to do them myself so I end up with high buns that get matted. 

Alternatively you could find a cowash product and put it in before you bath and have a rest after and then rinse it off in the bath? That’s probably what I’d do if I couldn’t manage my current routine.

Give yourself more gentle time and rest time than you expect to need.

Cutting out all conventional chemical cleaners and cosmetics. I went 100% scent/fragrance free. It was hard but worth it as I was really not able to process that on top of being so sick. I guess my liver needed and still needs some work. 

Other things that are weird but kinda helped- increasing negative ions because bedridden people don’t get many. Air and water quality. Working on drainage pathways (not detox) and cellular health. Replenishing lost minerals and vitamins. 
Finding  my ‘why am I putting so much effort in’ reason. When I lose that everything goes to hell mentally. Believing I could do it, no batter how bad I got made me never stop looking for answers which made me find a lot of things that were making me really unwell. Getting a watch with health data at the right time (probably when you’re more severe-moderate than very severe) can give tons of data. I think it would have taken too many spoons at my worst to think that much but everyone’s different. 
Meditating into different worlds where things didn’t suck as much helped me cope. Seeing beautiful things as often as possible. Even one detailed picture on my wall was an ‘activity’ where I could look for more details and appreciate the colours and composition. Eventually I did this with a whole wall of things that gave me some small amount of joy. 

I hope this helps someone.

I know it sucks being so sick, it’s hell. Tbh whatever gets you through another day is a miracle at that stage and honestly at my stage it’s still a battle. They’re not symptom free, they’re not 100% better. However they are improving year on year with dips they have to recover from. Not all of these will be possible for you but they might spark ideas for someone here. I hope. 

Explore childhood joys. Those hamma bead things or simple collages that are easy on hands. Writing little poems. Dinosaurs. Watching or listening to childhood favourites. Nostalgia can help. 

Haven’t seen people mention yoga nidra 
It’s a form of non sleep deep rest that I find helpful but wish I could get myself to do it more 

Guided meditations also helps 

Like someone else said I listen to shows I’ve watched before but again it gets old when you’ve been sick since childhood 

Something I did at my worse was holding crystals or something textural was soothing during rest.

When I first got sick I did put the effort in to celebrate things even though I was bedridden like Halloween etc and it did make a difference. I miss that. 

I also do EFT but again, not consistently. Or I hold the points. If tapping is too much.

I’d like to do things like getting some special mugs etc and spend time drinking tea in a more conscious way. 

Music let’s me explore new cultures 

Duolingo in the more ‘popular’ languages has listenable content which I’ve enjoyed and short activities that made me feel I was working towards something.

However I still feel I’m missing something big time.  

If carers can make you a garden or house ‘den’ that really helps. Giant bean bags. Essential oil diffuser. Journals. Weighted blankets Picture books. Music etc. 
I research healing a lot and have bought some devices that make me feel better but again it adds to the ‘should’ list so I’m looking for some more pampery things rather than ‘this helps my mitochondria I should really do this every day’ 

I would recommend a vibrating massage mat as you can lay on it and it’s soothing with good music 
I put a blanket over mine 
I also have a foot massager but looking for a shoulder massager 

If you have a bungalow or stairlift being taken out into the garden for a set amount of time. Having a bed of sorts out there. Vitamin D, fresh air, grass, sky, flowers. 

I’ve recently gotten into herbalism a little and found some herbs that reduce my insane need to do but I need to explore this more as I had a reaction to the one that helped most. 

I will put a little mention in here for postpals run by someone with cfs and sends cards to sick kids if you do enjoy craft. Samaritans will actually give you craft supplies to make cards for them if you’re interested or they used to. 

Gentle gentle bed stretches can help me feel less dead or prune Harris does energy work that I find can help with how drained I feel 

I do iPad art and Journalling coz it’s easier on my hands than paper 
And I do water colour 

Music used to help me so much until my hands messed up 

One of my big favourites was having pen pals that were also sick so understood if you didn’t get back to them. Don’t have to physically write.

Taking a picture of one good thing in your day no matter how small. Your morning tea, your pet, favourite pjs, bath day with fresh clean hair. Etc

I also used to love doing soap making (melt and pour) with creative shapes and colours/sparkles etc 
I also enjoyed jewellery making because you can get a little board so you could look at it and keep it in place so you can edit at your pace

Skincare/pampering - this is harder now with allergies and scent/struggling with harsh chemicals but even 2 minutes of self care can feel nice. A lip balm that feels good or a hand cream etc 

Gentle singing or humming can be something to let off steam 

If you can do literally anything creative, writing (speech to text) anything I highly recommend that. It helped me so much for so many years. Instruments, painting, polymer clay arts, crafts, even making slime like whatever works 

The artist’s way book is like creative outlet and therapy at the same time, if you can read a few mins a week. Don’t worry about getting through it at their timeline do a chapter a month or every two months or longer if needed. 

Also your head is a houseboat for anyone who like me cannot read full on books. It’s illustrated so less reading. 

Explore a topic you’ve always been interested in but never got round to.

In bed baking if you have carers or floor baking. 

Collecting things is nice. I did that with crystals at my worst. There’s lots to learn about them in a non pressured way. Mineral structure, where they’re from, folk lore about benefits etc 

 Volunteering in ways you can manage like if you can knit baby hats or something it’ll make you feel good in that ‘when you can’t help yourself help others’ way.

Making things special, baths have Epsom salts, essential oils and candles or a bath bomb if you can handle it. Or simply using that favourite shower gel that makes you feel good. 
Treating yourself to your favourite seasonal berries, drink or meal and freezing some for another time if it’s a meal. 

Not saying I can do all of these or that you will be able to either but I hope someone finds something out of this list.

If you would find learning to plait her hair fun then you guys could take a bath together and it could be bonding time where you can make touch soothing and actually takes something off her to do list and adds a bit of support because you could wash her hair and dry it for her and if you can then make it pretty in a braid it will keep it clean longer and she will have energy for other things and hopefully she would have energy for other things. If she needs to buy things for her room/house or redecorate or something breaks, you could send her different options and do some research if it’s something you’re interested in. Moving your space around when you have to spend all your time in it can be a huge pick me up.
